interfaceDesign: type tickKind int, consts tickBusy (zero value) | tickIdle | tickWaiting
type tickState struct { kind tickKind; count int } — comparable with ==
Supervisor gains an unexported lastReported tickState field
testFactory gains an output *bytes.Buffer field plus outputLines()/outputCount(text) test helpers

selfReview.item: Every public method has an intention-revealing name
Cyclomatic complexity < 7 on all new functions
selfReview.note: classify has the most branches (4 return paths, 1 level deep); confirmed via golangci-lint gocyclo (min-complexity 7, clean) and manual count — all new funcs are 2-4
tickState wraps the (kind, count) pair instead of two loose return values, so announce's == comparison stays a single check
the two printed line formats are the only literals, each used once, matching the spec's exact wording

selfReview.item: Dependency direction verified: nothing in inner layers imports from outer layers
selfReview.note: idle.go adds no new import; classify/waitingCount/hasUnshippedOrder take only map[string]*OrderState, per architecture-notes.md's structural decision — no Repository/TreeOpener/PullRequests/Intake can reach them

simpleDesign.note: go test ./internal/factory/... passes, including all 7 new idle_test.go cases and every pre-existing test
tickBusy as the zero value documents itself: a fresh Supervisor's first busy tick needs no sentinel
waitingPhases is one lookup table shared by waitingCount, matching inbox.go's itemsFor phase list (noted as an unenforced cross-check in architecture-notes.md)
no new package, no interface, no flag — one new file plus a two-line call-site change in Tick()

keyDecisions.decision: Put all idle/waiting classification and print-once logic in a new internal/factory/idle.go rather than supervisor.go
keyDecisions.reasoning: follows this package's existing one-concern-per-file convention (start.go, finish.go, replay.go, inbox.go), per architecture-notes.md

keyDecisions.decision: classify/waitingCount/hasUnshippedOrder take only map[string]*OrderState, never Dependencies/Repository/TreeOpener/Intake
keyDecisions.reasoning: makes the NFR ('no extra git or filesystem pass per tick', 'never call Inbox() or re-read intake') an enforced property of the function signature rather than a discipline to remember

keyDecisions.decision: tickKind's zero value is tickBusy, so tickState{} is the silent state
keyDecisions.reasoning: a fresh Supervisor's first busy tick stays silent with no separate 'never reported' sentinel

keyDecisions.decision: reportTickState() is the last step of Tick(), called only after a successful startWork, and re-derives orders via its own s.Orders() call
keyDecisions.reasoning: matches existing precedent — settleEnded, advanceFinishLine, and startWork already each call s.Orders() independently within one Tick(); the NFR targets Inbox()'s git/filesystem calls and re-reading intake, not the local ledger read, which stays well inside those bounds

notesForQa: idle_test.go covers: a fresh supervisor's idle line; the once-per-entry rule across consecutive idle ticks; a gate halt and a parked order each counting as waiting; a second order entering a waiting phase re-printing with the incremented count; leaving waiting (approval resumes the run) printing nothing, then re-entering idle once the order ships re-prints; a retrying order (before its backoff) printing nothing, per the spec's resolved Open Question; and Supervisor.Once() applying the same once-per-entry rule across two separate invocations.

go test ./internal/factory/... passes (full suite, 16s). golangci-lint run ./internal/factory/... reports one pre-existing, unrelated errcheck finding in units_test.go:163 (a file this change did not touch) — no issues in idle.go, idle_test.go, supervisor.go, or fixture_test.go.

Coverage: idle.go's new functions are 100% covered except reportTickState's s.Orders()-error branch (a one-line error forward, 80% on that function); the identical idiom is already uncovered at several sites in this same package (e.g. start.go's own s.Orders() error forward, and several pre-existing error branches in supervisor.go) — this matches established convention rather than introducing a new gap. Aggregate changed-line coverage is well above the 85% floor.
